correctness.rationale: For three candidates, strong nonnesting forces a unique optimal singleton A and a unique disjoint optimal pair BC (otherwise each pair meets some optimal singleton). In ballot variables (p,q,r,u,v,w,t,e) for A,B,C,AB,AC,BC,ABC,empty, strict scores imply v-w>=3,u-w>=3 and q,r>=p+2; hence n >= e+3p+3w+t+10 >=10. Equality forces p=w=t=e=0, q=r=2,u=v=3. Direct harmonic scores are A=6,B=C=5 for singletons, and BC=10, AB=AC=19/2 for pairs, giving unique disjoint winners. Ordering ballots B-only,AB,AC,C-only makes each approval interval. Independently enumerated exactly 19,448 anonymous profiles through n=10 over seven nonempty ballot types; none below ten and three at ten, matching the analytic all-n proof.

originality.rationale: PAV house nonmonotonicity is classical, including smaller tie-sensitive examples and much larger tie-independent witnesses. Important exact overlap: Brill-Freeman-Janson-Lackner published in Example 7.1 of their 2023/2024 Phragmen methods study the SAME ten-ballot multiset up to candidate relabeling, explicitly for leximax- and var-Phragmen rules, not PAV. Therefore the ten-voter pattern itself is PRIOR, not a novel witness. The surviving original statement is sharp PAV-specific MINIMALITY among all profiles, complete minimal-layer rigidity and voter-interval PAV implication; the inspected older examples and methods do not state/prove that minimum. Qualified PASS rests on that narrower nonimplied result.

value.rationale: Strong set-valued failure of nesting is a natural robust version of house monotonicity, avoiding artefacts from tie-breaking. A globally sharp smallest electorate and exact complete extremizer classification are motivated invariants; the voter-interval condition shows a structured preference domain does not restore the property, a distinction from score-value concavity.

final_claim: Among exactly three candidates under unweighted harmonic PAV, strong tie-independent nonnesting between optimal 1-seat and 2-seat committees requires at least ten voters, with exactly three anonymous labeled minimal profiles forming one candidate-renaming orbit and a voter-interval representative.
limitations: Exactly three candidates, unweighted voters, harmonic PAV, and strong tie-independent nonnesting; the ten-voter witness is already published for other voting rules.
The theorem does not establish minimum for ordinary tie-dependent failures or more candidates.
